strings.name: Peter Beck
strings.role: Rocket Lab founder, chairman, president and CEO
strings.summary: Peter Beck moved from precision-engineering apprenticeship and research into space entrepreneurship, founding Rocket Lab and developing launch, satellite and spacecraft businesses. His leadership shapes the company; rockets, engines and missions are achievements of engineering teams and partners.
strings.coverageNote: Reviewed through November 17, 2026. Birth year is unconfirmed. Academic appointment and degree, reaching space and orbit, launch count and success count, operating cash flow and profit, and Neutron targets and completed flights are distinguished.
strings.influence.rationale: Founded Rocket Lab, advancing small launch vehicles and commercial space systems in New Zealand and globally.
strings.facts.f1.label: Technical training
strings.facts.f1.value: Trained as an apprentice at Fisher & Paykel rather than entering through a university degree; appointed adjunct professor at Auckland in 2019.
strings.facts.f2.label: Limits of current developments
strings.facts.f2.value: On November 9, 2026 the company targeted Neutron’s first launch no earlier than 2027; backlog, cash flow and targets do not establish realized profit or completed flights.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Commercial launch and space systems
strings.highlights.h1.text: Developed Rocket Lab from rocket research into launch services and spacecraft; engineering achievements are not all attributed to him personally.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Industry and education
strings.highlights.h2.text: Helped develop New Zealand’s space industry and received educational recognition; an adjunct appointment does not mean completing a doctorate.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Company reports 100th Electron launch
strings.timeline.t1.text: Rocket Lab reports this mission succeeded and Beck thanks the team; the 100th launch does not mean all 100 launches succeeded.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Receives New Zealand knighthood
strings.timeline.t2.text: Named a Knight Companion of the New Zealand Order of Merit in the King’s Birthday Honours for aerospace, business and education services.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Rocket Lab goes public through merger
strings.timeline.t3.text: Combines with Vector Acquisition and begins Nasdaq trading as RKLB through a SPAC business combination.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Receives adjunct professorship
strings.timeline.t4.text: The University of Auckland announces his appointment in aerospace engineering, recognizing practical and industry contributions.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Electron first reaches orbit
strings.timeline.t5.text: Still Testing launches from Māhia, New Zealand, deploying satellites; distinct from the first test flight in 2017.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Launches Ātea-1
strings.timeline.t6.text: Leads early rocket-launch work; company and honours accounts record reaching space, separate from Electron’s later orbital missions.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Founds Rocket Lab
strings.timeline.t7.text: Establishes the space company, gradually building rocket, launch-site and spacecraft capabilities.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Begins engineering apprenticeship
strings.timeline.t8.text: According to the official company biography, starts precision-engineering training at Fisher & Paykel before moving into machinery and product design.
